blindSpots: Subagent-internal waste. `scripts/meta-week/lib/census.mjs` filters every detector to `lane === "main"`; a subagent's own re-reads, dead ends and loops are invisible, and only its `totalTokens` is charged. Measure: run the same three detectors over subagent lanes, and compute each agent's totalTokens against how much of its result the parent ever quotes or acts on.

Waste with no operator prompt and no system event to anchor on. Every detector hangs off a prompt, a block, or a compaction, so autonomous stretches, /loop runs, cron routines and background tasks are structurally unreachable. Measure: anchor on artifacts instead of prompts — spend between two commits, tokens per surviving diff line; flag any span with high spend and zero durable output (no commit, no PR, no file that survives).

Output that was produced and then never used. No detector asks whether anything was kept: the deleted `feat/phase5-report-body-mirror` branch, discarded agent results, rewritten specs all score zero. Measure: diff-survival — for each file written in a window, does its content still exist at HEAD 7 days later; for each branch, was it merged; for each Agent result, is it ever quoted or acted on afterward.

The waste usually sits outside the fixed window. Windows are forward-looking (30 min after a continue, 60 after a compaction) or prev-prompt-to-correction, and skeptics refuted 27 episodes largely because the window caught the remediation, not the defect (the wrong claim, the six-way dispatch, the earlier ignored stop all precede it). Measure: anchor backwards — from a retraction, string/semantic-match its subject to the earliest turn that asserted it and charge that span; from a TaskStop, walk back to the Agent calls it killed and charge the dispatch.

Corrections that never appear as an operator prompt. `unreadCandidates` only regex-matches USER text, so the vida episode's real correction — the assistant's own "The user is right, and I was wrong: dadb073" — was missed while a routine follow-up was flagged instead. Measure: detect corrections in ASSISTANT text ("I was wrong", "I overstated", "let me verify rather than assert") and charge the span back to the claim being retracted.

Slash commands and tool-generated lines counted as operator turns. `same-turn-many-sessions` normalizes text and needs only 3 sessions in 2 minutes, so `/model`, `/compact` and IDE open-file notices dominate; all three same-turn nominations were config commands. Measure: exclude slash-command, hook and IDE-generated prompts before grouping, and require the turn to carry a substantive instruction.

Real cross-session duplication. Matching by exact normalized prompt text in a 2-minute window cannot see two sessions doing the same job worded differently hours apart — exactly the six duplicate-fix PRs of 2026-07-09. Measure: overlap of touched file paths, branch prefixes and PR titles across concurrent sessions in the same repo within a day, not prompt text.

Instrument-blind waste — work that is finished, green and useless (a gate that can never pass, a VERDICT grepping the wrong command). It emits no stop, no compaction and no correction, and it is this repo's signature failure mode. Measure: per-check pass/fail history — any gate that has only ever passed, or only ever failed, since introduction is unproven; pair with whether any mutation ever made it bite.

Time and cache cost, as distinct from token cost. `minutes` includes idle (one refuted window had a 13-hour gap), polling sleeps and until-loops cost wall-clock with no tokens, and `cacheRead` is charged to whatever window it lands in. Measure: split sessions into active spans (gap > 10 min = idle) before any rate, report blocked-on-polling wall-clock separately, and use cache-read per unit of new output rather than raw cache-read.

Redundant re-verification. Re-running a full suite or re-screenshotting with nothing changed in between is never flagged, because the files were not re-read and no prompt marks it. Measure: identical Bash command with identical result and no Edit to the files under test between the two runs.
